paras: The pursuit and capture of Calvin Baker was a May 1903 manhunt for a 15-year-old Black boy accused of attempting to assault a five-year-old girl near Phenix City, Alabama. A Columbus, Georgia, dispatch said he would "very likely be lynched on the spot" if the posse caught him. He was instead captured by a ruse and carried to Opelika, the Lee county seat.

Baker worked in the butcher shop of a man named as "Mr. Theftford" in one report and "Mr. Richard Thedford" in the other. According to the first dispatch, Baker enticed the butcher's five-year-old daughter out of the family residence near the shop at about eight o'clock on the night of May 20. The follow-up dispatch placed the alleged attempt at "Knight's Station" rather than in "Pheonix City."

Baker fled after the accusation, and by the next day, when the matter "just gained publicity," a posse was "scouring the woods" for him. Thedford followed him to Crawford, Alabama, ten miles east, where the boy had applied for work on the farm of a Mr. Foster.

At about six o'clock on the morning of May 22, Foster sent Baker into a crib and locked the door behind him. Baker was brought to Phenix City that morning "with a rope tied around his neck to prevent him from escaping." That afternoon he was carried to Opelika, the county seat of Lee county.
No report of an indictment or trial appears in the coverage, and no officers are named in the search or capture.

Coverage came only from white papers carrying Columbus dispatches. The Hattiesburg Daily Progress ran the first on May 22 under the headline "A NEGRO BRUTE," stating the accusation as fact and forecasting a lynching without comment. The Savannah Morning News put the capture on its front page on May 23 as "LED WITH A ROPE ABOUT HIS NECK," describing Baker as "Charged With a Serious Crime" but calling the incident "the attempted outrage." No Black-press account of the case was found.

reader.title: Pursuit and capture of Calvin Baker
bases: A posse hunted a Black boy accused of an attempted assault and the wire said he would 'very likely be lynched on the spot' if caught (A1); he was instead captured by a farmer and taken to the county seat (A2), so this is at most a threatened lynching.
Two separate Columbus dispatches of May 21 and May 22 agree on the accused, his age, the accusation and the flight (A1, A2), though both come from the same Columbus wire source.

accounts.label: Columbus wire, May 21
accounts.gist: A posse was scouring the woods for Baker, who had fled after an alleged attempted assault the night before; if caught he would 'very likely be lynched on the spot'.

accounts.label: Columbus wire, May 22
accounts.gist: Baker was captured by a ruse near Crawford, brought to Phenix City with a rope around his neck, and carried to Opelika that afternoon.

framing.detail: The Hattiesburg paper headed the Columbus wire 'A NEGRO BRUTE' and 'Mob Scouring the Woods', predicting a lynching without comment.
The Savannah Morning News ran the capture on page one as 'LED WITH A ROPE ABOUT HIS NECK', calling the accusation 'a Serious Crime' and 'the attempted outrage'.

record_check.dossier: Threatened lynching: a posse manhunt with a reported likelihood of lynching, ending in capture and transfer to the county seat.
At large on May 21; captured at 6 a.m. May 22 and carried to Opelika that afternoon.
Pursuit, capture by ruse, led with a rope around his neck, transfer to Opelika.
Black ('a fifteen year old negro boy').
No county named for the offense; Baker was taken to the Lee county seat, Opelika, which implies Lee county jurisdiction.
Two white papers (Hattiesburg, May 22; Savannah, May 23); no Black-press coverage found.

info: Alleged attempted assault on the night of Wednesday, May 20, 1903 ('about 8 o'clock last night' in a May 21 dispatch; 'Wednesday night'); capture at 6 a.m. on May 22.

Alleged offense at 'Pheonix City' near the butcher's residence (A1) or at 'Knight's Station' (A2); capture near Crawford, Ala., 'ten miles east of the city'; Baker brought to Phenix City, then to Opelika.
Calvin Baker, a 15-year-old 'negro boy', employed in the butcher's shop.
Accused of attempting to assault the five-year-old daughter of the butcher, Mr. 'Theftford' (A1) or 'Richard Thedford' (A2), after enticing her from the residence.
A posse ('Mob' in the headline) searched the woods; the capture was made by the girl's father, who tracked Baker to Crawford, and a farmer, Mr. Foster, who locked him in a crib.
Baker was taken to Opelika alive; no report of a trial or of any lynching was found.

quotes: A posse is out scouring the woods for Calvin Baker, a fifteen year old negro boy who attempted an assault on the little five year old daughter of Mr. Theftford
Baker has fled and if caught will very likely be lynched on the spot.
